title: Cold rebuild: XOR two byte arrays
summary: Rebuild XOR two byte arrays from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **XOR two byte arrays** in *XOR and the one-time pad*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.explain: `1100 ^ 1010 = 0110`, which is 6. XOR with the key again restores 12.

steps.title: Rebuild XOR two byte arrays cold
prompt: Write `byte[] Xor(byte[] a, byte[] b)` that returns a new array where `result[i] = a[i] ^ b[i]`. If the lengths differ, throw `ArgumentException`: a pad shorter than the message is not a one-time pad.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
